points.name: 〜でも (demo) — even / at least / or something
points.shortDescription: Three uses: 'even [noun]' (inclusive extreme), 'how about [noun]' (soft suggestion), and universal question words.
points.formation: Noun + でも  |  Question word + でも (どこでも, 何[なん]でも, 誰[だれ]でも)
points.explanation:
でも is one of those small words that punches well above its weight. Attached to nouns, it does three distinct things — and all three come up naturally in everyday Japanese.

Use 1 — 'even': この問題[もんだい]は子[こ]どもでも解[と]けますよ (Even a child can solve this). By choosing an extreme or surprising case (a child!) and saying でも, you imply the whole range: if even a child can, surely everyone can. The argument goes from the edge of the spectrum to the center. 私[わたし]でも分[わ]かりました (Even I understood it) is a common humble way of saying something is very clear.

Use 2 — casual suggestion ('or something'): お茶[ちゃ]でも飲[の]みませんか (How about we have some tea?). でも makes the suggestion deliberately vague and low-pressure — tea, or coffee, or whatever. It's an extremely natural way to propose something without being demanding, and you'll use it constantly in social situations.

Use 3 — universal question words: question words + でも = no-exception universals.
何[なん]でも (anything), 誰[だれ]でも (anyone), どこでも (anywhere), いつでも (anytime), 何[なん]でもいい (anything's fine).
Compare: 何[なん]でも (with positive verb) vs 何[なに]も (with negative verb). 何[なん]でも食[た]べます (I eat anything) vs 何[なに]も食[た]べません (I don't eat anything). でも + positive; も + negative.
rules: Noun + でも = even [noun] (includes an extreme case to make a broader point)
Noun + でも = 'or something / how about' (casual, low-pressure suggestion)
Question word + でも = universal: 何[なん]でも (anything), 誰[だれ]でも (anyone), どこでも (anywhere)
Universal でも works with AFFIRMATIVE verbs — contrast with 何[なに]も/誰[だれ]も which need negatives
Context distinguishes the three uses: 子[こ]どもでも (even a child) vs お茶[ちゃ]でも (tea or something)

examples.japanese: この問題[もんだい]は子[こ]どもでも解[と]けますよ。
examples.romaji: Kono mondai wa kodomo demo tokemasu yo.
examples.english: Even a child can solve this problem.

examples.japanese: 疲[つか]れましたね。コーヒーでも飲[の]みませんか。
examples.romaji: Tsukaremashita ne. Koohii demo nomimasen ka.
examples.english: You must be tired. How about having some coffee or something?

examples.japanese: このサービスはだれでも無料[むりょう]で使[つか]えます。
examples.romaji: Kono saabisu wa dare demo muryou de tsukaemasu.
examples.english: Anyone can use this service for free.

examples.japanese: いつでも気軽[きがる]に連絡[れんらく]してください。
examples.romaji: Itsudemo ki garu ni renraku shite kudasai.
examples.english: Please feel free to contact me anytime.

points.flashcardAnswer: 'Even [noun]' / 'how about [noun]?' / question word + でも = universal (anything/anyone/anywhere).

practice.prompt: What does でも mean when expressing 'even'?
choices: but / however (conjunction between clauses)
even / even something as expected as (particle: noun + でも)
should do (obligation)
approximately / about
practice.explanation: Noun + でも = even X (even something as noteworthy or extreme as X). 子供[こども]でも分[わ]かる = even a child can understand. でも here is a particle expressing 'even the minimum/extreme case applies'.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Even a child can do this'?
choices: 子供[こども]がこれができる。
子供[こども]もこれができる。
子供[こども]でもこれができる。
子供[こども]こそこれができる。
practice.explanation: でも = even: 子供[こども] + でも = even a child. これができる = can do this. 子供[こども]でもこれができる = even a child can do this. でも highlights the extreme/minimum case that still applies.

practice.prompt: What is the DIFFERENT use of でも as a CONJUNCTION?
choices: even X
but / however (linking contrasting clauses)
should / must, with no exceptions in modern standard Japanese.
approximately
practice.explanation: でも as conjunction = but / however (contrasting two statements). 雨[あめ]が降[ふ]っています。でも、出[で]かけます = it's raining. But/however, I'll go out. This conjunction でも is separate from the particle でも (even).

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Even on a Sunday, he works'?
choices: 日曜日[にちようび]にも彼[かれ]は働[はたら]く。
日曜日[にちようび]でも彼[かれ]は働[はたら]く。
日曜日[にちようび]こそ彼[かれ]は働[はたら]く。
日曜日[にちようび]だけ彼[かれ]は働[はたら]く。
practice.explanation: Noun + でも = even : 日曜日[にちようび] + でも = even on Sunday. 日曜日[にちようび]でも彼[かれ]は働[はたら]く = even on Sundays he works. でも highlights that Sunday (when most don't work) is no exception.

practice.prompt: Which means 'Even an expert would find this difficult'?
choices: 専門家[せんもんか]にこれは難[むずか]しい。
専門家[せんもんか]はこれが難[むずか]しい。
専門家[せんもんか]でもこれは難[むずか]しい。
専門家[せんもんか]もこれが難[むずか]しい。
practice.explanation: Noun + でも = even . 専門家[せんもんか] + でも = even an expert. これは難[むずか]しい = this is difficult. 専門家[せんもんか]でもこれは難[むずか]しい = even an expert would find this difficult.

practice.prompt: Which correctly uses でも for 'even the smallest things matter'?
choices: 小[ちい]さいことにも関係[かんけい]がある。
小[ちい]さいことでも大切[たいせつ]です。
小[ちい]さいことこそ大切[たいせつ]です。
小[ちい]さいことだけ大切[たいせつ]です。
practice.explanation: Noun/phrase + でも = even . 小[ちい]さいこと + でも = even small things. 大切[たいせつ]です = are important. 小[ちい]さいことでも大切[たいせつ]です = even small things are important.

practice.prompt: Which question uses でも to mean 'anything / whatever' (offering options)?
choices: 何[なに]かを飲[の]みますか？
何[なん]でも飲[の]みますか？
何[なに]も飲[の]みません。
何[なん]でも飲[の]みましょう。
practice.explanation: question-word + でも = whatever / anything. 何[なん]でも = anything/whatever. 何[なん]でも飲[の]みますか = will you drink anything (whatever you like)? question-word + でも is a common pattern for open-ended permission.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Anyone can join this club'?
choices: だれかこのクラブに入[い]れます。
だれもこのクラブに入[い]れます。
だれでもこのクラブに入[い]れます。
だれこそこのクラブに入[い]れます。
practice.explanation: だれ + でも = anyone (whoever). だれでもこのクラブに入[い]れます = anyone can join this club. Q-word + でも = whoever/whatever — open, inclusive, no restrictions.

practice.prompt: Which means 'Even if it's something small, a gift makes people happy'?
choices: 小[ちい]さいものでも、プレゼントは人[ひと]を喜[よろこ]ばせる。
小[ちい]さいものも、プレゼントは人[ひと]を喜[よろこ]ばせる。
小[ちい]さいものだけ、プレゼントは人[ひと]を喜[よろこ]ばせる。
小[ちい]さいものこそ、プレゼントは人[ひと]を喜[よろこ]ばせる。
practice.explanation: でも = even if (concessive): 小[ちい]さいもの + でも = even if it's something small. プレゼントは人[ひと]を喜[よろこ]ばせる = a gift makes people happy. でも after a noun creates 'even if it's ' concessive meaning.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'You can go anywhere you like'?
choices: どこかに行[い]けます。
どこにでも行[い]けます。
どこにも行[い]けません。
どこだけに行[い]けます。
practice.explanation: どこ + にでも = anywhere (to any place). どこにでも行[い]けます = you can go anywhere (no restriction on destination). Q-word + particle + でも = wherever/whatever.

practice.prompt: Which demonstrates でも after a TE-FORM (even if / whether or not)?
choices: 食[た]べても大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]。(Even if you eat, it's fine.)
食[た]べてもいい。(It's okay to eat — permission.)
食[た]べるでも大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]。
食[た]べたでも大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]。
practice.explanation: Te-form + も = 〜ても = even if. 食[た]べても = even if  eat. 食[た]べても大丈夫[だいじょうぶ] = it's fine even if you eat. This is the ても (even if) construction, using でも through combination.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Even water can be dangerous in excess'?
choices: 水[みず]でも飲[の]みすぎると危険[きけん]です。
水[みず]も飲[の]みすぎると危険[きけん]です。
水[みず]こそ飲[の]みすぎると危険[きけん]です。
水[みず]だけ飲[の]みすぎると危険[きけん]です。
practice.explanation: Noun + でも = even . 水[みず] + でも = even water. 飲[の]みすぎると危険[きけん]です = is dangerous if drunk too much. 水[みず]でも飲[の]みすぎると危険[きけん]です = even water is dangerous in excess.

practice.prompt: Which means 'I'll eat anything as long as it's not raw fish'?
choices: 生魚[せいぎょ]以外[いがい]なら何[なん]でも食[た]べます。
生魚[せいぎょ]でもなんでも食[た]べます。
生魚[せいぎょ]さえあれば何[なん]でも食[た]べます。
生魚[せいぎょ]以外[いがい]なら何[なに]かを食[た]べます。
practice.explanation: 何[なん]でも = anything. 生魚[せいぎょ]以外[いがい] = except raw fish. 何[なん]でも食[た]べます = will eat anything. 生魚[せいぎょ]以外[いがい]なら何[なん]でも食[た]べます = I'll eat anything except raw fish.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'When I was a child, I would eat anything' (no restriction)?
choices: 子供[こども]のとき、何[なに]かを食[た]べた。
子供[こども]のとき、何[なん]でも食[た]べた。
子供[こども]のとき、何[なに]も食[た]べなかった。
子供[こども]のとき、何[なん]だけを食[た]べた。
practice.explanation: 何[なん]でも = anything / whatever. 何[なん]でも食[た]べた = ate anything (no restrictions). Q-word + でも = inclusive 'any-' word.

practice.prompt: What does いつでも mean?
choices: never
sometimes
always / at any time
right now only
practice.explanation: いつ + でも = いつでも = anytime / always / whenever. いつでも来[き]てください = please come anytime. Q-word + でも = 'any-' word that is open and inclusive with no restriction.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Even adults sometimes make mistakes'?
choices: 大人[おとな]もときどきミスをします。
大人[おとな]でもときどきミスをします。
大人[おとな]こそときどきミスをします。
大人[おとな]だけときどきミスをします。
practice.explanation: Noun + でも = even . 大人[おとな] + でも = even adults. 大人[おとな]でもときどきミスをします = even adults sometimes make mistakes.

practice.prompt: Which means 'Even if it's cold, I'll go for a walk'?
choices: 寒[さむ]くても、散歩[さんぽ]に行[い]きます。
寒[さむ]くでも、散歩[さんぽ]に行[い]きます。
寒[さむ]いでも、散歩[さんぽ]に行[い]きます。
寒[さむ]いでも散歩[さんぽ]に行[い]きます。
practice.explanation: い-adj te-form + も = 〜くても = even if . 寒[さむ]くて + も = 寒[さむ]くても = even if cold. 寒[さむ]くても散歩[さんぽ]に行[い]きます = even if it's cold, I'll go for a walk.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Please call me anytime'?
choices: いつかに電話[でんわ]してください。
いつもに電話[でんわ]してください。
いつでも電話[でんわ]してください。
いつにでも電話[でんわ]してください。
practice.explanation: いつでも = anytime (no time restriction). いつでも電話[でんわ]してください = please call anytime. Q-word + でも = open, no restriction.

practice.prompt: Which uses でも as a CONJUNCTION (but/however)?
choices: 子供[こども]でも分[わ]かる。
でも、まだやれる。
何[なん]でも食[た]べます。
どこでも行[い]けます。
practice.explanation: でも as a standalone conjunction (but/however): でも、まだやれる = but/however, I can still do it. This でも is different from the particle でも (even) and Q-word + でも (any-). Conjunction でも comes at the START of a sentence.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Even the smallest mistake can be important'?
choices: 小[ちい]さなミスでも重要[じゅうよう]なことがある。
小[ちい]さなミスもそれが重要[じゅうよう]なことがある。
小[ちい]さなミスこそが重要[じゅうよう]なことがある。
小[ちい]さなミスだけが重要[じゅうよう]なことがある。
practice.explanation: Noun + でも = even . 小[ちい]さなミス + でも = even a small mistake. 重要[じゅうよう]なことがある = can be important. 小[ちい]さなミスでも重要[じゅうよう]なことがある = even a small mistake can be important.

points.name: 〜て初[はじ]めて (te hajimete) — not until / only after doing
points.shortDescription: Only after doing X for the first time did Y become clear — the turning-point realization.
points.formation: Verb (て-form) + 初[はじ]めて + result/realization
points.explanation:
〜て初[はじ]めて is the grammar of the turning point — the moment when an experience makes something true or clear that wasn't before. It means 'not until X / only after X did Y.'

日本[にほん]に住[す]んで初[はじ]めて、文化[ぶんか]の違[ちが]いを実感[じっかん]しました: 'It wasn't until I actually lived in Japan that I really felt the cultural differences.' Before living there: the realization was absent. After the experience: it arrived. The experience was the enabling condition.

The 初[はじ]めて here carries its literal meaning — 'for the first time' — and that first-time quality is essential. This is the grammar of experiences you can't get second-hand: the first time you had children, the first time you went abroad, the first time you failed publicly. Something only experience can teach.

The pattern often appears in moments of grateful realization or hard-won insight. 子[こ]どもを持[も]って初[はじ]めて、親[おや]のありがたさがわかった: 'It wasn't until I had children that I understood how much I owe my parents.' The emotional weight of て初[はじ]めて comes from the implicit 'before this, I didn't know' sitting behind every sentence.

Simple formation: て-form of verb + 初[はじ]めて + result or realization.
rules: Verb (て-form) + 初[はじ]めて = not until doing X / only after experiencing X for the first time
The result in the main clause was only possible after the て clause experience happened
初[はじ]めて retains its literal meaning 'for the first time' — first-time experience enables the outcome
Carries a turning-point feel: before X, not the case; after X, now true
Common with realizations, gratitude, and insights that only lived experience can provide

examples.japanese: 日本[にほん]に住[す]んで初[はじ]めて、文化[ぶんか]の違[ちが]いを実感[じっかん]しました。
examples.romaji: Nihon ni sunde hajimete, bunka no chigai wo jikkan shimashita.
examples.english: It wasn't until I lived in Japan that I truly felt the cultural differences.

examples.japanese: 子[こ]どもを持[も]って初[はじ]めて、親[おや]のありがたさがわかりました。
examples.romaji: Kodomo wo motte hajimete, oya no arigatasa ga wakarimashita.
examples.english: It wasn't until I had children that I understood how grateful I should be to my parents.

examples.japanese: 失敗[しっぱい]して初[はじ]めて、失敗[しっぱい]の大切[たいせつ]さを学[まな]んだ。
examples.romaji: Shippai shite hajimete, shippai no taisetsu-sa wo mananda.
examples.english: Only after failing did I learn the importance of failure.

examples.japanese: 海外[かいがい]に出[で]て初[はじ]めて、日本[にほん]の良[よ]さに気[き]づきました。
examples.romaji: Kaigai ni dete hajimete, Nihon no yosa ni kizukimashita.
examples.english: It wasn't until I went abroad that I noticed what's great about Japan.

points.flashcardAnswer: Only after experiencing X for the first time did Y become possible — the turning-point pattern.

practice.prompt: What does 〜て(から)はじめて mean?
choices: started doing X
first time doing X ever
it was only after doing X that Y became apparent/possible for the first time
will do X first, then Y
practice.explanation: 〜てはじめて = it was only after doing X that . 外国[がいこく]に行[い]って初[はじ]めて、日本[にほん]の良[よ]さが分[わ]かった = it was only after going abroad that I first understood Japan's greatness. Realization that came only AFTER the experience.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'It was only after becoming a parent that I understood my parents' hardships'?
choices: 親[おや]になってはじめて、親[おや]の苦労[くろう]が分[わ]かった。
親[おや]になってから、親[おや]の苦労[くろう]が分[わ]かった。
親[おや]になっていて、親[おや]の苦労[くろう]が分[わ]かった。
親[おや]になるまでに、親[おや]の苦労[くろう]が分[わ]かった。
practice.explanation: Te-form + はじめて: なって (te-form of なる) + はじめて = only after becoming. 親[おや]になってはじめて + 親[おや]の苦労[くろう]が分[わ]かった = only after becoming a parent did I first understand my parents' hardships.

practice.prompt: What is the KEY FEELING expressed by 〜てはじめて?
choices: regret about something not done
surprise / realization that X was needed for Y to be understood (often can't know Y without X experience)
frustration about a repeated action — textbooks treat this as an absolute rule.
expectation about the future
practice.explanation: 〜てはじめて expresses REALIZATION — you couldn't know/understand Y until you actually experienced X. 失[うしな]ってはじめて大切[たいせつ]さが分[わ]かる = only after losing something do you understand its value. A common Japanese proverb-like structure.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'It was only after getting sick that I understood the importance of health'?
choices: 病気[びょうき]になってから、健康[けんこう]の大切[たいせつ]さが分[わ]かった。
病気[びょうき]になったとき、健康[けんこう]の大切[たいせつ]さが分[わ]かった。
病気[びょうき]になってはじめて、健康[けんこう]の大切[たいせつ]さが分[わ]かった。
病気[びょうき]になるまで、健康[けんこう]の大切[たいせつ]さが分[わ]かった。
practice.explanation: 〜てはじめて for realization: 病気[びょうき]になって (te-form) + はじめて = only after getting sick. 健康[けんこう]の大切[たいせつ]さが分[わ]かった = understood the importance of health. Only getting sick made this understanding possible.

practice.prompt: Which means 'Only after graduating did I realize how fun school was'?
choices: 卒業[そつぎょう]してから、学校[がっこう]が楽[たの]しかったと分[わ]かった。
卒業[そつぎょう]してはじめて、学校[がっこう]が楽[たの]しかったと気[き]づいた。
卒業[そつぎょう]したとき、学校[がっこう]が楽[たの]しかったと気[き]づいた。
卒業[そつぎょう]するまで、学校[がっこう]が楽[たの]しかったと気[き]づいた。
practice.explanation: 〜てはじめて: 卒業[そつぎょう]して (te-form) + はじめて = only after graduating. 気[き]づいた = noticed/realized. 卒業[そつぎょう]してはじめて、学校[がっこう]が楽[たの]しかったと気[き]づいた = only after graduating did I realize school was fun.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'You can only understand loneliness after experiencing it'?
choices: 孤独[こどく]を経験[けいけん]してはじめて、孤独[こどく]が分[わ]かる。
孤独[こどく]を経験[けいけん]してから、孤独[こどく]が分[わ]かる。
孤独[こどく]を経験[けいけん]すると、孤独[こどく]が分[わ]かる。
孤独[こどく]を経験[けいけん]したとき、孤独[こどく]が分[わ]かる。
practice.explanation: 〜てはじめて for general truths: 経験[けいけん]して (te-form) + はじめて = only after experiencing. 孤独[こどく]が分[わ]かる = understand loneliness. Only by experiencing it can you truly understand it.

practice.prompt: What distinguishes 〜てはじめて from 〜てから?
choices: They are completely identical
〜てから = after X, then Y (sequential); 〜てはじめて = only after X does Y become possible/understood for the first time (realization/first-time)
〜てから = simultaneous actions; 〜てはじめて = past action, regardless of context or politeness level.
〜てはじめて = more formal; 〜てから = casual
practice.explanation: てから = sequential (after X, then Y happens — neutral). てはじめて = only AFTER X, Y became possible/understood FOR THE FIRST TIME (realization/special nuance). 卒業[そつぎょう]してから = after graduating (neutral sequence). 卒業[そつぎょう]してはじめて = only after graduating (realization).

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Only after losing something do you know its value'?
choices: 失[うしな]ってはじめて、その価値[かち]が分[わ]かる。
失[うしな]ってから、その価値[かち]が分[わ]かる。
失[うしな]ったとき、その価値[かち]が分[わ]かる。
失[うしな]うまで、その価値[かち]が分[わ]かる。
practice.explanation: 〜てはじめて: 失[うしな]って (te-form) + はじめて = only after losing. 価値[かち]が分[わ]かる = understand its value. 失[うしな]ってはじめてその価値[かち]が分[わ]かる = only by losing it do you first understand its value.

practice.prompt: Which means 'Only after working as a teacher did I understand what education truly is'?
choices: 先生[せんせい]として働[はたら]いてから、教育[きょういく]とは何[なに]か分[わ]かった。
先生[せんせい]として働[はたら]いてはじめて、教育[きょういく]とは何[なに]か分[わ]かった。
先生[せんせい]として働[はたら]いたとき、教育[きょういく]とは何[なに]か分[わ]かった。
先生[せんせい]として働[はたら]くまで、教育[きょういく]とは何[なに]か分[わ]かった。
practice.explanation: 〜てはじめて: 働[はたら]いて (te-form) + はじめて = only after working. 教育[きょういく]とは何[なに]か分[わ]かった = understood what education is. Only the experience of being a teacher revealed this understanding.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Only after traveling abroad did I become interested in my own country'?
choices: 海外[かいがい]に旅行[りょこう]してから、自分[じぶん]の国[くに]に興味[きょうみ]を持[も]った。
海外[かいがい]に旅行[りょこう]してはじめて、自分[じぶん]の国[くに]に興味[きょうみ]を持[も]った。
海外[かいがい]に旅行[りょこう]したとき、自分[じぶん]の国[くに]に興味[きょうみ]を持[も]った。
海外[かいがい]に旅行[りょこう]するまで、自分[じぶん]の国[くに]に興味[きょうみ]を持[も]った。
practice.explanation: 〜てはじめて: 旅行[りょこう]して (te-form) + はじめて = only after traveling. 興味[きょうみ]を持[も]った = became interested. The travel experience created the realization/interest in one's own country.

practice.prompt: Which situation is BEST described by 〜てはじめて?
choices: After finishing work, I went home
When I came home, dinner was ready — this is true in both spoken and written Japanese.
Only after having children did I understand my parents' love
I went to the store and came back
practice.explanation: 'Only after having children did I understand parents' love' = perfect 〜てはじめて. The experience (having children) unlocked a new understanding (parents' love). This realization was impossible without the experience — the key feature of てはじめて.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Only when you try it do you realize how hard it is'?
choices: やってみてはじめて、どれほど難[むずか]しいか分[わ]かる。
やってみてから、どれほど難[むずか]しいか分[わ]かる。
やってみたとき、どれほど難[むずか]しいか分[わ]かる。
やってみると、どれほど難[むずか]しいか分[わ]かる。
practice.explanation: 〜てはじめて: やってみて (te-form of やってみる) + はじめて = only after trying. どれほど難[むずか]しいか分[わ]かる = understand how difficult it is. Only by trying do you first realize the difficulty.

practice.prompt: Which means 'Only after getting lost did I realize how important maps are'?
choices: 迷子[まいご]になってから、地図[ちず]の重要性[じゅうようせい]が分[わ]かった。
迷子[まいご]になったとき、地図[ちず]の重要性[じゅうようせい]が分[わ]かった。
迷子[まいご]になってはじめて、地図[ちず]の重要性[じゅうようせい]が分[わ]かった。
迷子[まいご]になるまで、地図[ちず]の重要性[じゅうようせい]が分[わ]かった。
practice.explanation: 〜てはじめて: 迷子[まいご]になって (te-form) + はじめて = only after getting lost. 地図[ちず]の重要性[じゅうようせい]が分[わ]かった = understood the importance of maps. Getting lost was the experience that revealed this.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'I only understood when I read the book'?
choices: 本[ほん]を読[よ]んでから分[わ]かった。
本[ほん]を読[よ]んでいて分[わ]かった。
本[ほん]を読[よ]んでみると分[わ]かった。
本[ほん]を読[よ]んではじめて分[わ]かった。
practice.explanation: 〜てはじめて: 読[よ]んで (te-form) + はじめて = only after reading. 分[わ]かった = understood. 本[ほん]を読[よ]んではじめて分[わ]かった = it was only after reading the book that I understood.

practice.prompt: Which pattern correctly uses 〜てはじめて with a general truth?
choices: 彼女[かのじょ]に会[あ]ったとき、彼女[かのじょ]が美[うつく]しいと思[おも]った。
困[こま]ってはじめて、人[ひと]の親切[しんせつ]が分[わ]かる。
大学[だいがく]に入[はい]ってから、友達[ともだち]ができた。
試験[しけん]が終[お]わってから、遊[あそ]ぶ。
practice.explanation: 困[こま]ってはじめて、人[ひと]の親切[しんせつ]が分[わ]かる = only when you're in trouble do you first understand people's kindness. This is a general truth expressed with 〜てはじめて. The difficulty (X) reveals the kindness (Y).

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Only after apologizing did I feel better'?
choices: 謝[あやま]ってから、気分[きぶん]が良[よ]くなった。
謝[あやま]ってはじめて、気分[きぶん]が良[よ]くなった。
謝[あやま]ったとき、気分[きぶん]が良[よ]くなった。
謝[あやま]るまでに、気分[きぶん]が良[よ]くなった。
practice.explanation: 〜てはじめて: 謝[あやま]って (te-form) + はじめて = only after apologizing. 気分[きぶん]が良[よ]くなった = felt better. The act of apologizing was what made the first feeling of relief possible.

practice.prompt: Which means 'Only after making a mistake do you learn'?
choices: 失敗[しっぱい]してから、人[ひと]は学[まな]ぶ。
失敗[しっぱい]したとき、人[ひと]は学[まな]ぶ。
失敗[しっぱい]してはじめて、人[ひと]は学[まな]ぶ。
失敗[しっぱい]するまで、人[ひと]は学[まな]ぶ。
practice.explanation: 〜てはじめて: 失敗[しっぱい]して (te-form) + はじめて = only after failing. 人[ひと]は学[まな]ぶ = people learn. 失敗[しっぱい]してはじめて人[ひと]は学[まな]ぶ = it is only by failing that people learn. Classic てはじめて wisdom statement.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Only after trying Japanese cooking did I appreciate it'?
choices: 日本料理[にほんりょうり]を作[つく]ってから、その良[よ]さが分[わ]かった。
日本料理[にほんりょうり]を作[つく]ったとき、その良[よ]さが分[わ]かった。
日本料理[にほんりょうり]を作[つく]ってはじめて、その良[よ]さが分[わ]かった。
日本料理[にほんりょうり]を作[つく]るまで、その良[よ]さが分[わ]かった。
practice.explanation: 〜てはじめて: 作[つく]って (te-form) + はじめて = only after making/trying. その良[よ]さが分[わ]かった = appreciated its goodness. The hands-on experience was necessary for the appreciation.

practice.prompt: What type of verb MOST commonly precedes はじめて?
choices: The te-form of verbs describing an EXPERIENCE that creates new understanding
The ta-form of verbs
The dict-form of verbs, and the rule applies to every sentence type.
Nouns + の
practice.explanation: Te-form of experience verbs + はじめて: 経験[けいけん]して、失[うしな]って、なって、行[い]って, etc. The experience (te-form) is what enables the new understanding (second clause). Typically experiential or process verbs.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'Only after living alone did I appreciate home cooking'?
choices: 一人暮[ひとりぐ]らしをしてから、手料理[てりょうり]のありがたさが分[わ]かった。
一人暮[ひとりぐ]らしをしたとき、手料理[てりょうり]のありがたさが分[わ]かった。
一人暮[ひとりぐ]らしをしてはじめて、手料理[てりょうり]のありがたさが分[わ]かった。
一人暮[ひとりぐ]らしをするまでに、手料理[てりょうり]のありがたさが分[わ]かった。
practice.explanation: 〜てはじめて: 一人暮[ひとりぐ]らしをして (te-form) + はじめて = only after living alone. 手料理[てりょうり]のありがたさが分[わ]かった = appreciated home cooking. Living alone was the necessary experience for this realization.

points.name: 〜かな / 〜かしら — I wonder (self-directed question)
points.shortDescription: Self-directed wondering — 'I wonder if / when / what…' — thinking aloud, not asking anyone.
points.formation: Plain form + かな  |  Plain form + かしら (feminine)
points.explanation:
かな and かしら are sentence-final particles for wondering out loud. They turn a statement into an inward-facing question — not directed at a listener, but at yourself, or into the air.

明日[あした]は晴[は]れるかな: 'I wonder if it'll be sunny tomorrow.' The speaker isn't asking anyone — they're musing. This is very different from 明日[あした]は晴[は]れますか?, which asks a specific person. かな makes the wondering self-contained.

かな is casual and gender-neutral — you'll hear it constantly in everyday conversation. かしら is traditionally associated with a softer, more feminine register, though it's used by all genders in some contexts and literary styles. Both are perfectly natural in casual speech.

These particles beautifully capture the gentle uncertainty of everyday life: wondering if the shop is open, if someone has arrived, if the weather will hold. They're also useful for expressing modest wishes or mild worries without being direct: もう少[すこ]し上手[じょうず]になれるかな (I wonder if I can get a little better…) carries a wistful quality that a direct statement wouldn't.

かなあ is an extended form (the あ adds a long, trailing murmur) that deepens the wondering feeling: どうすればいいんだろうなあ…  The more drawn-out the vowel, the more you're sinking into the thought.
rules: Plain form + かな = I wonder [whether/when/what…] (casual, all genders)
Plain form + かしら = I wonder (softer; traditionally feminine register)
Self-directed — thinking aloud, not asking a specific listener
Carries gentle uncertainty, wistful wondering, or mild doubt
Extended form: かなあ (longer trailing vowel deepens the wondering, reflective feeling)

examples.japanese: 明日[あした]、晴[は]れるかな。
examples.english: I wonder if it'll be sunny tomorrow.

examples.japanese: あの人[ひと]、だれだろう。知[し]り合[あ]いかな。
examples.romaji: Ano hito, dare darou. Shiriai kana.
examples.english: Who is that person, I wonder. Could be someone I know.

examples.japanese: いつになったら日本語[にほんご]が上手[じょうず]になれるかしら。
examples.romaji: Itsu ni nattara nihongo ga jouzu ni nareru kashira.
examples.english: I wonder when I'll ever get good at Japanese.

examples.japanese: 田中[たなか]さん、もう帰[かえ]ったのかな。電気[でんき]が消[き]えてるけど。
examples.romaji: Tanaka-san, mou kaetta no kana. Denki ga kieteru kedo.
examples.english: I wonder if Tanaka-san has already left. The lights are off.

points.flashcardAnswer: Thinking aloud — 'I wonder if / when…' — self-directed musing, not a direct question.

practice.prompt: What does 〜かな mean?
choices: a strong assertion
I wonder / I hope (gentle self-directed musing)
because / since
if only / even though
practice.explanation: 〜かな = I wonder / I hope (casual, spoken, often self-directed musing). 明日[あした]は晴[は]れるかな = I wonder if it'll be sunny tomorrow. かな expresses gentle uncertainty or wistful wondering, typically used by male/neutral speakers.

practice.prompt: How does 〜かしら differ from 〜かな?
choices: They are completely identical
かしら = typically more feminine/soft; かな = more gender-neutral/slightly masculine
かしら = formal; かな = informal
かしら = for questions to others; かな = for self-questions only
practice.explanation: Both かな and かしら express wondering/musing, but: かしら = traditionally more feminine or soft. かな = more gender-neutral (used by male speakers, neutral speakers). In modern Japanese, both are used, but this distinction exists in traditional/formal contexts.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'I wonder if he's coming today' (using かな)?
choices: 彼[かれ]は今日[きょう]来[く]るかな。
彼[かれ]は今日[きょう]来[く]るかしら。
彼[かれ]は今日[きょう]来[く]るかも。
彼[かれ]は今日[きょう]来[く]るだろう。
practice.explanation: Dict-form + かな = I wonder if . 来[く]る + かな = I wonder if  come. 彼[かれ]は今日[きょう]来[く]るかな = I wonder if he's coming today. (Self-directed wondering).

practice.prompt: Which correctly uses かしら to say 'I wonder if this is correct'?
choices: これは正[ただ]しいかしら。
これは正[ただ]しいかな。
これは正[ただ]しいだろう。
これは正[ただ]しいか。
practice.explanation: Plain form + かしら = I wonder if . 正[ただ]しい + かしら = I wonder if  correct. かしら follows adjective plain form directly. Often associated with a more feminine/soft wondering tone.

practice.prompt: What is the DIFFERENCE between 〜かな/かしら and 〜か (question)?
choices: They are the same thing
〜か = direct question to someone else; 〜かな/かしら = self-directed musing/wondering (not asking others)
〜か = formal; 〜かな = informal — and this holds in every register, formal or casual.
〜か = past; 〜かな = future
practice.explanation: 〜か = direct question to someone else (asks for an answer). 〜かな/かしら = self-directed wondering (musing to oneself or half-aloud, not expecting an answer from the listener). 来[く]るか？(Are you coming?) vs 来[く]るかな (I wonder if  come).

practice.prompt: Which correctly expresses 'I wonder if the package has arrived'?
choices: 荷物[にもつ]は届[とど]いたかな。
荷物[にもつ]は届[とど]いたか。
荷物[にもつ]は届[とど]くかな。
荷物[にもつ]は届[とど]いたかしら。
practice.explanation: Ta-form + かしら = I wonder if  has happened. 届[とど]いた + かしら = I wonder if  has arrived. Both 荷物[にもつ]は届[とど]いたかな (option 1) and 届[とど]いたかしら (option 3) are correct; correctIndex=3 labels かしら.

practice.prompt: Which situation best illustrates かな?
choices: A student asks the teacher a question, with no exceptions in modern standard Japanese.
Someone wonders aloud to themselves while looking at the sky
Making a formal request
Asserting a fact to someone else
practice.explanation: Someone wonders aloud while looking at the sky (e.g., 明日[あした]、雨[あめ]が降[ふ]るかな = I wonder if it'll rain tomorrow) = classic かな. It's a self-directed musing said out loud or to oneself — not a request for information from others.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'I wonder if she likes me' (using かしら)?
choices: 彼女[かのじょ]は私[わたし]が好[す]きかな。
彼女[かのじょ]は私[わたし]が好[す]きかしら。
彼女[かのじょ]は私[わたし]が好[す]きか。
彼女[かのじょ]は私[わたし]が好[す]きだろう。
practice.explanation: Plain form adjective + かしら: 好[す]き + かしら = I wonder if  likes . 彼女[かのじょ]は私[わたし]が好[す]きかしら = I wonder if she likes me (soft, feminine wondering).

practice.prompt: Which means 'I wonder if this restaurant is open today'?
choices: このレストランは今日[きょう]開[ひら]いているかな。
このレストランは今日[きょう]開[ひら]いているか？
このレストランは今日[きょう]開[ひら]いているかも。
このレストランは今日[きょう]開[ひら]いているだろう。
practice.explanation: 〜ているかな = I wonder if  is . 開[ひら]いている + かな = I wonder if  is open. このレストランは今日[きょう]開[ひら]いているかな = I wonder if this restaurant is open today.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'I wonder what I should do' (using かな)?
choices: どうすればいいかな。
どうすればいいか？
どうすればいいかしら。
どうすればいいだろう。
practice.explanation: どうすればいいかな = I wonder what I should do / what would be best. Question word + かな = self-directed wondering with question-word. どうすればいいかな is very common in casual self-reflection.

practice.prompt: Which form does かな/かしら attach to for past events?
choices: Masu-stem
Te-form
Ta-form (past plain)
Dictionary form
practice.explanation: Ta-form + かな/かしら for past events: 来[き]たかな = I wonder if  came. 届[とど]いたかしら = I wonder if  arrived. Ta-form before かな/かしら for wondering about past events.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'I wonder if I can make it to the meeting'?
choices: 会議[かいぎ]に間[ま]に合[あ]うかな。
会議[かいぎ]に間[ま]に合[あ]うか？
会議[かいぎ]に間[ま]に合[あ]うかも。
会議[かいぎ]に間[ま]に合[あ]うかしら。
practice.explanation: Dict-form + かしら: 間[ま]に合[あ]う + かしら = I wonder if I'll make it in time. 会議[かいぎ]に間[ま]に合[あ]うかしら = I wonder if I can make it to the meeting (soft feminine musing). Option 1 (かな) is also correct.

practice.prompt: Which means 'I wonder if the exam results are out'?
choices: 試験[しけん]の結果[けっか]が出[で]たかな。
試験[しけん]の結果[けっか]が出[で]たか？
試験[しけん]の結果[けっか]が出[で]たかも。
試験[しけん]の結果[けっか]が出[で]るかな。
practice.explanation: Ta-form + かな for past-event wondering: 出[で]た + かな = I wonder if  out (I wonder if the results were released). 試験[しけん]の結果[けっか]が出[で]たかな = I wonder if exam results have been released yet.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'I wonder if this kanji is correct' (using かな)?
choices: この漢字[かんじ]は正[ただ]しいかな。
この漢字[かんじ]は正[ただ]しいか？
この漢字[かんじ]は正[ただ]しいかも。
この漢字[かんじ]は正[ただ]しいかしら。
practice.explanation: Plain adjective + かな: 正[ただ]しい + かな = I wonder if  correct. この漢字[かんじ]は正[ただ]しいかな = I wonder if this kanji is correct (self-directed doubt/wondering).

practice.prompt: What is かな/かしら used for when directed AT a listener (not just oneself)?
choices: It cannot be used toward a listener — textbooks treat this as an absolute rule.
As a very soft/indirect suggestion to consider something: 行[い]ったらいいかな = wouldn't it be good to go?
As a polite command
As a way to refuse
practice.explanation: When directed at a listener, かな/かしら softens a suggestion or mild expectation: 行[い]ったらいいかな (said to someone) = wouldn't it be good to go? / I wonder if you should go. It's much softer than a direct recommendation.

practice.prompt: Which correctly expresses 'I wonder if it will snow tomorrow'?
choices: 明日[あした]、雪[ゆき]が降[ふ]るかな。
明日[あした]、雪[ゆき]が降[ふ]るかも。
明日[あした]、雪[ゆき]が降[ふ]るかしら。
明日[あした]、雪[ゆき]が降[ふ]るだろうか。
practice.explanation: Dict-form + かしら: 降[ふ]る + かしら = I wonder if it'll snow. 明日[あした]、雪[ゆき]が降[ふ]るかしら = I wonder if it'll snow tomorrow. (Option 1 with かな is equally correct; correctIndex=2 labels かしら.)

practice.prompt: Which means 'I wonder what time she'll come'?
choices: 彼女[かのじょ]は何時[なんじ]に来[く]るかな。
彼女[かのじょ]は何時[なんじ]に来[く]るか？
彼女[かのじょ]は何時[なんじ]に来[く]るかも。
彼女[かのじょ]は何時[なんじ]に来[く]るだろう。
practice.explanation: Q-word + dict-form + かな = I wonder . 何時[なんじ]に来[く]る + かな = I wonder what time  come. 彼女[かのじょ]は何時[なんじ]に来[く]るかな = I wonder what time she'll arrive.

practice.prompt: Which correctly says 'I wonder if there's a good method' (using かしら)?
choices: いい方法[ほうほう]があるかな。
いい方法[ほうほう]があるかしら。
いい方法[ほうほう]があるかも。
いい方法[ほうほう]があるか？
practice.explanation: Plain form + かしら: ある + かしら = I wonder if . いい方法[ほうほう]があるかしら = I wonder if there's a good method. Self-directed wondering about possibility.

practice.prompt: Which sentence pair shows the TYPICAL USAGE CONTRAST of かな vs かしら?
choices: 彼[かれ]は来[く]るかな。(man wondering) / 彼[かれ]は来[く]るかしら。(woman wondering)
かな = formal; かしら = informal (for any gender)
かな = for past; かしら = for future
They cannot both follow the same form
practice.explanation: Traditional contrast: 彼[かれ]は来[く]るかな (man or neutral wondering) / 彼[かれ]は来[く]るかしら (woman or soft/feminine wondering). Both mean 'I wonder if he'll come'. This gender-register contrast is the classic distinction, though modern Japanese has blurred it somewhat.

practice.prompt: Which correctly uses かな to mean 'I wonder if I made a mistake'?
choices: 間違[まちが]えたかな。
間違[まちが]えるかな。
間違[まちが]えるかしら。
間違[まちが]えたかしら。
practice.explanation: Ta-form + かな for past wondering: 間違[まちが]えた + かな = I wonder if I made a mistake. 間違[まちが]えたかな = I wonder if I was wrong (self-questioning past action). Both option 1 and option 4 (かしら) are grammatically correct; correctIndex=0 labels かな.
